item.title: A haplotype reference panel constructed from 490,319 UK Biobank genomes improves genotype imputation for global populations.
item.author: Wienbrandt L, Prieß C, Schmöhl M, Neff V, Gretsova M, Torres G, Wacker EM, Franke A, Ellinghaus D.
item.description:
Here we constructed a genotype imputation reference panel from whole-genome sequencing data from 490,319 UK Biobank (UKB) participants 1 and enabled both standalone and cloud-based phasing and imputation through EagleImp 2 and EagleImp-RAP within the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform. The UKB reference panel achieves lower phasing switch error rates than the widely used TOPMed r3 panel (133,597 individuals) for all global superpopulations except AMR and for 25 of 26 1000 Genomes Project subpopulations. Imputation accuracy, measured by MAE, improved for 4 of 5 superpopulations and 12 subpopulations for variants with minor allele frequencies down to 0.01%. Estimated squared correlation further improved across all 5 superpopulations and 22 subpopulations, with the largest gains in East and South Asian populations. item.title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation.
item.author: Varshney A, Manickam N, Orchard P, Tovar A, Ventresca C, Zhang Z, Feng F, Mears J, Erdos MR, Narisu N, Nishino K, Rai V, Stringham HM, Jackson AU, Tamsen T, Gao C, Yang M, Koues OI, Welch JD, Burant CF, Williams LK, Jenkinson C, DeFronzo RA, Norton L, Saramies J, Lakka TA, Laakso M, Tuomilehto J, Mohlke KL, Kitzman JO, Koistinen HA, Liu J, Boehnke M, Collins FS, Scott LJ, Parker SCJ.
item.description:
Skeletal muscle tissue underlies several polygenic metabolic traits and diseases. Identifying their genetic mechanisms requires pinpointing cell types, regulatory elements, target genes and causal variants. Here we use genetic multiplexing to generate population-scale single-nucleus chromatin accessibility (single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq)) and transcriptome (single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq)) maps across 287 frozen human skeletal muscle biopsies. We identify 13 cell types and integrate genetic variation to discover >7,000 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and >100,000 chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) across cell types, including context-specific eQTL/caQTL with significant G × C interaction. item.title: Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization and TWAS.
item.author: Head ST, Bresnahan ST, Chang YH, Shah VM, Cole NR, Wu W, Bhattacharya A.
item.description:
Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, colocalization and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to contextualize genome-wide association study loci, yet the impact of upstream RNA-sequencing processing choices on these analyses remains critically unexplored. Two poorly characterized decisions include the transcriptomic reference annotation used for quantification of short-read RNA-sequencing samples, which defines transcript composition and structure, and the quantification method itself. Here, through a comprehensive analysis spanning 48 tissues in GTEx and 7 widely studied and diverse phenotypes, we find that these choices substantially affect eQTL detection and gene expression prediction with significant downstream impacts on colocalization and TWAS results. item.title: Near-complete assembly of wild emmer wheat unveils centromere reorganization during polyploid evolution.
item.author: Yi C, Liu Q, Shen L, Zhang J, Zhu C, Wang T, Han F, Liu Y.
item.description:
Wild emmer wheat (Triticum turgidum ssp. dicoccoides, BBAA), the wild progenitor of cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats, provides an important reference for investigating centromere reorganization during polyploidization and domestication. Here we generated a near-complete genome assembly of wild emmer wheat, including centromeric regions for all 14 centromeres. Comparative analyses with cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats revealed extensive variation in centromere-associated sequences and centromere-proximal structure, as well as distinct subgenome-associated patterns in the A and B subgenomes. The A subgenome was characterized by positional shifts and sequence turnover of CRW-rich centromere-derived blocks, whereas the B subgenome showed reduced CentT566 satellite abundance accompanied by localized retention or expansion on specific chromosomes. item.title: High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies.
item.author: Gerlach PA, Milind N, Spence JP, Pritchard JK.
item.description:
Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to identify genes involved in complex traits and to infer the direction of gene effects on traits. However, despite their popularity, it remains unclear how accurately TWAS recover the true direction of a gene's effect on a trait. Here we estimate the false sign rate of TWAS for plasma proteins, leveraging the expectation that increased gene expression should generally increase protein expression. We then extend this framework to complex traits, where loss-of-function burden tests provide the expected direction of effect. In both analyses, we observe high discordance with expectations, with TWAS showing a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits.
